answer: Knoll-terrace beacon decay bond: an agent stakes 70 credits on a knoll terrace plot and posts a reading. The signal decays 8 per epoch; the agent returns to forge a fresh one. Auditors recompute decay on the public table and burn reused readings. A first reading costs 38, rising 6 per fake, so 1,000 fakes cost 3,035,000, lock 70,000, against a 40,000 pool. Rented-beacon rings fail: each fake needs a terrace plot. Honest agents pay 38 once.
